skill.name: audit-before-i-tweet
skill.description: Review a finished tweet for missing context, unsupported claims, unintended interpretations, lost qualifiers, and voice consistency. Rank up to three fixes before publishing.
skill.summary: Audit a finished tweet and prioritize small fixes before publishing.
skill.author: prateeks367

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives: four identify Markdown tool names, and one misclassifies editorial guidance as system reconnaissance. No evidence found of command execution, credential access, exfiltration, or prompt injection in SKILL.md. Optional VoiceMOAT publishing is described with a preview and one-time confirmation; its implementation is not included.

- `score_voice_match` scores the draft from 0 to 100 against that profile,
- `improve_post` takes it through a deeper pass when step 6 finds three real
- `publish_post` sends it once you are happy, behind a preview and a one-time

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 81 uses Markdown backticks around get_voice_profile to describe an optional VoiceMOAT tool. This is documentation, not Ruby or shell execution.
Line 84 formats score_voice_match as an inline Markdown tool name and describes its scoring output. No executable expression or shell command appears.
Line 86 uses Markdown backticks to name improve_post in a description of optional draft revision. The surrounding prose contains no shell execution.
Lines 88-89 document publish_post with Markdown formatting and require a preview and one-time confirmation. The backticks do not execute a command.
Lines 43-45 ask whether readers could interpret a tweet differently from its intended meaning. This is editorial analysis, not host inspection or system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Short tweets can lose context, overstate claims, or expose identifiable people. This skill checks a finished draft and ranks up to three fixes before publishing.
actual_capabilities: Review whether a tweet makes sense without a bio, thread, or surrounding conversation.
Flag numbers needing sources, stories needing verification, and potentially identifiable people.
Identify unintended interpretations when a tweet is quoted or shared without context.
Check whether shortening removed qualifiers needed to keep a claim accurate.
Review voice consistency qualitatively; describe profile-based scoring when VoiceMOAT is connected.
Rank at most three fixes, identify clean checks, and recommend whether to post the draft unchanged.
limitations: Does not create a tweet from nothing or predict engagement and performance.
Cannot guarantee factual accuracy or privacy protection; users must verify sources and identifiable details.
Standalone voice review is qualitative and does not produce a numerical score.
VoiceMOAT tools require a connected Pro or Enterprise plan; this skill includes no connector implementation.

use_cases.title: Check a product announcement
use_cases.description: Review an announcement for unclear subjects, unsupported numbers, and missing qualifiers before posting.

use_cases.title: Review a client-related anecdote
use_cases.description: Check whether readers could identify a client or misinterpret a professional story.

use_cases.title: Prioritize final editorial fixes
use_cases.description: Review a finished brand tweet, preserve its voice, and return no more than three prioritized changes.

prompt_templates.title: Basic final review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this finished tweet before I post it: [draft]. Rank up to three fixes and say whether you would post it unchanged.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review a single completed draft.

prompt_templates.title: Claims and identification
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [draft] for unsupported claims and identifiable people. Use [sources] as context, and tell me what still needs verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review factual or professional claims.

prompt_templates.title: Context and qualifiers
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [draft] as a standalone screenshot. Compare it with [full thought] to find unintended readings or lost qualifiers. Rank only necessary fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review a shortened or sensitive statement.

prompt_templates.title: Voice-aware final decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [draft] against [my published posts]. If VoiceMOAT is connected, use its voice profile and scoring. Rank fixes; do not publish without confirmation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine editorial review with voice references or an available connector.

output_examples.input: Ready to post: Our tool cuts support costs by 50% for everyone. Evidence: one four-week customer pilot.
output: Fix 1: Replace 'for everyone' with the scope of the single customer pilot.
Fix 2: Name the source for the 50% figure and verify how support costs were measured.
Clean check: The subject is clear without surrounding context.
Decision: Revise the claim before posting.

output_examples.input: Final review: We moved our weekly planning meeting from Monday to Tuesday. For our team, that leaves Monday free for focused work.
output: Clean checks: The subject is clear, and 'for our team' preserves the claim's scope.
Clean checks: No numerical result or identifiable outside person appears in the draft.
Voice: No reference posts were supplied, so personal voice consistency remains unverified.
Decision: I would post this as written.

best_practices: Provide a finished draft and supporting sources for numbers or factual claims.
Supply the original thought when shortening may have removed important qualifiers.
Use your own published posts as voice references and review every suggested change before publishing.
anti_patterns: Requesting a new tweet from an empty brief instead of submitting a completed draft.
Treating the review as a performance forecast or guaranteed factual verification.
Rewriting the entire tweet when a small correction would resolve the issue.

faq.question: Does this skill write tweets from scratch?
faq.answer: No. It reviews finished drafts and prioritizes necessary fixes.

faq.question: What does the audit check?
faq.answer: It checks standalone context, claims, identifiable people, unintended interpretations, missing qualifiers, and voice consistency.

faq.question: How many fixes will I receive?
faq.answer: The skill requests at most three fixes, ordered by cost, plus clean checks and a posting recommendation.

faq.question: Will it predict engagement or give a score?
faq.answer: It does not predict engagement. Standalone review has no numerical score; a connected VoiceMOAT tool can provide voice-match scoring.

faq.question: Do I need VoiceMOAT?
faq.answer: No. Editorial checks work without it. Profile-based scoring and connected publishing require VoiceMOAT with a Pro or Enterprise plan.

faq.question: Does it publish automatically?
faq.answer: The file contains no publishing implementation. Its optional VoiceMOAT workflow describes publishing only after a preview and one-time confirmation.
